title: Art Sartorius et al. v. Presbytery of the Siouxlands
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the complaint on procedural grounds and ordered Presbytery to retry TE Gregory Lawrence on the same five-charge indictment. It did not determine his guilt or adopt the complainants’ doctrinal allegations.
first_summary: Teaching and ruling elders challenged Presbytery’s approval of TE Gregory Lawrence’s acquittal on five doctrinal charges. The SJC sustained the complaint because the trial commission admitted his post-indictment exculpatory writings while permitting him not to testify, preventing cross-examination. It remanded for a new trial on the same indictment, without deciding whether Lawrence was guilty.
summary: Teaching and ruling elders challenged Presbytery’s approval of TE Gregory Lawrence’s acquittal on five doctrinal charges. The SJC sustained the complaint on procedural grounds: the trial commission relied on his post-indictment exculpatory writings while he declined to testify, depriving the prosecution of cross-examination. The SJC ordered a new trial on the same indictment under specified evidentiary procedures. Because this was a complaint rather than an appeal, it did not reverse the acquittals into findings of guilt or decide the doctrinal merits.

sources.supports: Case identity, complaint procedure, judgment, adopted reasoning, retrial instructions, and adoption vote.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Caption and decision identify Case 2012-08 and the parties (printed p. 528, lines 13–19); the SJC adopted the amended decision 18–1 (printed p. 538, lines 256–258).
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint challenged Presbytery’s approval of five not-guilty judgments, alleging doctrinal and trial-process errors (printed pp. 532–533, lines 85–115).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC found serious procedural error because post-indictment exculpatory statements were treated as testimony without cross-examination, and ordered a new trial (printed pp. 533–536, lines 113–197).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The complaint procedure permitted annulment or a new trial, not conversion of acquittals into guilt; later guilty or not-guilty judgments remained subject to appeal or complaint (printed pp. 535–536, lines 158–201). The separate concurrence expressly disclaimed prejudging guilt (printed p. 543, lines 318–334).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference. Case 2008-14 appears only as procedural history (printed p. 529, lines 39–45).

source_limits: The source supplies the full adopted decision and a concurring opinion but no substantive dissenting opinion.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged approval of five acquittals and the evidentiary defect.
score_reasons.decision: States the procedural success, remand, and absence of a guilt determination.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains that uncross-examined exculpatory writings were improperly treated as testimony.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the complaint-versus-appeal limitation and retrial remedy.
score_reasons.fidelity: Distinguishes the adopted procedural holding from doctrinal allegations and the separate concurrence.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the challenge, ruling, reason, and remedy.

verification_notes: Rechecked the judgment and retrial instructions at lines 113–201. The final summary clarifies that the complaint was sustained only on procedural grounds, that all five charges were to be retried, and that the SJC made no doctrinal guilt determination.
